decree: قرار الجمعية العمومية للهيئة السعودية للمهندسين (إقرار اللائحة التنفيذية)

amendment_history.decree: قرار الجمعية العمومية للهيئة السعودية للمهندسين
amendment_history.note: الإصدار المتداول حالياً (32 مادة، 6 فصول بلا أبواب) -- إقرار اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الهيئة السعودية للمهندسين، مؤرخ على غلافه '1445هـ / 2024م' فقط، دون رقم اجتماع أو تاريخ إقرار محدد داخل نص اللائحة ذاته. لم يُعثر على نسخة أرشيفية سابقة لهذا الملف بعينه لمقارنتها (لقطة أرشيفية واحدة فقط بتاريخ 25/6/2025م عبر Wayback Machine CDX)؛ لذلك لا يمكن تحديد أي مادة بعينها بأنها 'معدلة' عن إصدار سابق دون تخمين، فجرى اعتبار كل المواد الاثنتين والثلاثين 'أصلية' بوصفها النص الساري الحالي الموثّق، لا بوصف مطابقتها الحرفية لأي إصدار داخلي سابق (انظر known_unresolved_discrepancies).

chapter_structure.title_ar: تعريف الألفاظ والعبارات الواردة في النظام واللائحة (م1).
أجهزة الهيئة الخمسة: الجمعية العمومية، مجلس الإدارة، الأمانة العامة، الشعب الهندسية، فروع الهيئة.

sections.title_ar: انعقاد الجمعية العمومية العادية وإجراءاتها (م2)؛ حالات انعقادها الاستثنائي (م3).
تشكيل مجلس الإدارة من عشرة أعضاء، تحديد الجهات الحكومية الممثلة، اختيار الرئيس ونائبه، ومدة العضوية (م4).
إنشاء الشعب الهندسية بقرار من مجلس الإدارة (م7).
فتح فروع أو مكاتب للهيئة داخل المملكة (م8)؛ تشكيل لجان تنسيقية في المناطق التي لا فروع لها (م9).

chapter_structure.label_ar: الفصل الثالث: انتخابات مجلس إدارة الهيئة
chapter_structure.title_ar: لجنة الإشراف على الانتخابات وتشكيلها واختصاصاتها (م10)؛ إجراءات وآليات الترشح وأسلوب التعريف بالمترشح وضوابط الحملة الانتخابية وأسلوب الانتخاب (م11)؛ النظر في الشكاوى والاعتراضات والتظلمات (م12-م14)؛ موعد الانتخابات وإبلاغ الأعضاء (م15-م16)؛ شروط الترشح لعضوية مجلس الإدارة (م17)؛ لجنة الطعون واختصاصاتها (م18-م20)؛ إعادة الانتخابات (م21)؛ فوز المترشحين وإقرار النتائج (م22-م23)؛ إفصاح عضو مجلس الإدارة عن تعارض المصالح (م24)؛ خلو مقعد عضو منتخب (م25).
اعتبار العضوية بعد إتمام إجراءات التسجيل (م26)؛ منح العضوية الفخرية (م27).
إدارة أموال الهيئة وإيداعها (م28)؛ المقابل المالي عن خدمات الهيئة (م29).
قبول التبرعات والهبات واستثمار الأموال (م30)؛ حظر التصرف في الأموال خارج أهداف الهيئة (م31)؛ نفاذ اللائحة من تاريخ إقرارها من الجمعية العمومية (م32).

verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: a direct curl fetch of https://www.saudieng.sa/Admin/NPSCERules/sce-executive-regulations.pdf this pass failed with a TLS connection reset (consistent with this corpus's established pattern for saudieng.sa direct scraping). The Wayback Machine CDX metadata API (https://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx) was queried first and confirmed exactly ONE archived capture of this exact URL: timestamp 20250625074825 (25 Jun 2025), status 200, mimetype application/pdf, length 1,016,913 bytes -- matching the prior research's own cited '2025-06-25' snapshot. The content-serving Wayback path (https://web.archive.org/web/20250625074825/https://www.saudieng.sa/Admin/NPSCERules/sce-executive-regulations.pdf) was then fetched via direct curl over the pre-configured proxy and SUCCEEDED this pass (returning the full 16-page, ~1MB PDF byte-identical to the CDX-recorded digest/length), so no Scribd-mirror or r.jina.ai fallback was strictly needed for text acquisition -- though both were still attempted for independent cross-verification and both proved unavailable this pass (see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key sce_reg_scribd_and_jina_fallbacks_unavailable).

DUAL-PIPELINE TEXT EXTRACTION: this PDF's embedded Arabic text stream is stored in raw visual (right-to-left glyph-position) character order without correct Unicode logical ordering or bidi markup -- a known class of Arabic-PDF authoring artifact distinct from, and more severe than, ordinary justified-text kashida spacing. A naive 'pdftotext -layout' or 'pdfplumber .extract_text()' pass on this file therefore initially yields visually mirrored / reversed-word-order text. This track's generator resolves this via a from-scratch word-level reconstruction (see the reusable extraction logic documented in this track's own build tooling): for each PDF page, words are extracted via pdfplumber with their x/y bounding boxes, grouped into lines by y-coordinate, each line's words are sorted by DESCENDING x-coordinate (rightmost-first, matching RTL reading order), and each individual word's own character stream is reversed BEFORE Unicode NFKC normalization (reversing after normalization was tried first and found to corrupt multi-codepoint decompositions such as the lam-alef ligature, silently swapping 'لا' into 'ال' -- reversing before normalization avoids this). Embedded digit runs (ASCII and Arabic-Indic) and bracket/parenthesis characters are then corrected back to their proper left-to-right reading order and orientation (both had been incorrectly flipped by the whole-word reversal). This reconstruction was cross-checked against an entirely independent poppler 'pdftotext -layout' extraction of the SAME archived PDF (a different underlying parsing engine, PDF-object-stream reader, and text-layout heuristic) -- the two extractions agree, word-for-word, on the full 32-article text after normalization, which this track treats as strong internal corroboration against a tool-specific transcription error (though both necessarily read the SAME single archived copy of the file, so this is a parsing cross-check, not an independent-source cross-check in the sense of two different hosts serving the text).

STRUCTURE: 32 articles across 6 named فصول (chapters; this regulation has no أبواب) -- الفصل الأول: التعريفات (م1); الفصل الثاني: أجهزة الهيئة (م2-م9, itself subdivided into 5 lettered subsections أ-هـ for the General Assembly, Board of Directors, Secretariat-General, engineering divisions, and Council branches); الفصل الثالث: انتخابات مجلس إدارة الهيئة (م10-م25, by far the longest chapter, covering the election-supervision committee, candidacy procedures, campaign conduct rules, the appeals committee, and vacancy filling); الفصل الرابع: التسجيل والعضوية (م26-م27); الفصل الخامس: الأحكام المالية (م28-م29); الفصل السادس: أحكام ختامية (م30-م32). No article carries an inline topic title distinct from its chapter/subsection heading; section_ar carries the chapter/subsection context instead, consistent with this corpus's established convention for sources lacking inline per-article titles (see this corpus's saudi_engineers, awqaf_law, nazaha_law, and accounting_auditing_law precedent).

LEGAL STATUS / AMENDMENT HISTORY: this regulation is a Council-internal instrument issued under the base law's own General-Assembly rule-making delegation -- it is NOT BOE-catalogued and carries no per-article 'تعديلات المادة' changelog mechanism analogous to the one this corpus's own saudi_engineers (base law) track relied on for its Articles 1 and 6. Only ONE archived capture of this exact file was found (see above); no earlier edition of this same instrument was located to diff against. All 32 articles are therefore recorded as 'اصلية' (original/current), meaning verified-current text of the single consolidated 1445H/2024G edition as hosted by the regulator -- NOT an affirmative claim that every article's wording is identical to whatever earlier internal edition(s) preceded this reissuance (see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key sce_reg_no_prior_edition_found_for_diff, and key sce_reg_general_assembly_meeting_number_unconfirmed for the specific '20th General Assembly, 2024' attribution this pass could not independently confirm).

DISAMBIGUATION FROM THE SIBLING engineering_practice_regulation TRACK: this pass specifically fetched and read (via its own Wayback snapshot) a second, textually and structurally distinct 'اللائحة التنفيذية' PDF hosted in the SAME saudieng.sa directory (Admin/NPSCERules/67.pdf) to confirm it is NOT this track's subject matter -- it is instead اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية (Implementing Regulation of the Law of the Practice of Engineering Professions), issued by Ministerial Resolution No. (4400942200/4) dated 26/5/1445هـ and published in Umm Al-Qura Gazette No. 5013 (16/6/1445هـ) -- a government ministerial regulation implementing individual-engineer licensing/accreditation/discipline under the SEPARATE base law نظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية (Royal Decree م/36, 19/4/1438هـ). See known_unresolved_discrepancies, key sce_reg_disambiguation_from_engineering_practice_regulation, for the full comparison. This track ingests ONLY the Council's own organizational implementing regulation (sce-executive-regulations.pdf).

No legal text is altered beyond whitespace normalization and stripping decorative/justification tatweel (كشيدة) characters not forming part of the 'هـ' Hijri-era-marker idiom (consistent with this corpus's established tatweel-stripping convention). Several confirmed source-level spelling/typesetting artifacts (an inconsistent hamza-under-alef orthographic style throughout, three isolated one-off misspellings, and one stray duplicate-numeral artifact in Article 29) are preserved VERBATIM rather than silently corrected -- see known_unresolved_discrepancies for the full account of each. Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation performed on the Arabic text (English descriptions in this note and in document_en/issuing_authority_en are for indexing only). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: This track is the Saudi Council of Engineers' OWN internal implementing regulation for its organizing statute (نظام الهيئة السعودية للمهندسين, Royal Decree م/36, 26/9/1423هـ -- already tracked in this corpus at sources/saudi_engineers/), issued by the Council's own General Assembly under that law's Article 5(2) ('إقرار اللوائح التنفيذية لنظام الهيئة') and Article 7(3) (Board's proposal power), hosted directly by the Council at saudieng.sa/Admin/NPSCERules/sce-executive-regulations.pdf and dated on its own cover '1445هـ / 2024م'. It governs the HEIGHT'S internal organs (اجهزة الهيئة): the General Assembly, Board of Directors composition and elections, the Secretariat-General, engineering divisions (الشعب الهندسية), branches, registration/membership, and the Council's own finances -- 32 articles, 6 chapters, no per-article ministerial/BOE amendment mechanism. THIS IS DISTINCT from a separate, currently-in-force instrument independently confirmed this pass via its own archived copy (Wayback snapshot of saudieng.sa/Admin/NPSCERules/67.pdf, captured 27 May 2025): اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية (Implementing Regulation of the Law of the Practice of Engineering Professions), which is issued by MINISTERIAL RESOLUTION No. (4400942200/4) dated 26/5/1445هـ and published in the Umm Al-Qura official gazette No. 5013 dated 16/6/1445هـ -- i.e. a government ministerial regulation implementing the SEPARATE practice/licensing/discipline law (نظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية, Royal Decree م/36 dated 19/4/1438هـ, a distinct decree despite the identical number -- see the base law track's own known_unresolved_discrepancies key saudi_engineers_decree_number_collision_m36), governing professional accreditation, the accreditation committee, and disciplinary penalties for individual engineers and firms. The two implementing-regulation instruments differ in EVERY structural respect confirmed this pass: issuing mechanism (Council General Assembly resolution vs. Ministerial Resolution), publication channel (Council's own website only vs. Umm Al-Qura official gazette), subject matter (the Council's own internal governance organs vs. individual-engineer licensing/discipline), and file identity (sce-executive-regulations.pdf vs. 67.pdf). This track ingests ONLY the former (the Council's own organizational implementing regulation); the latter is the separate engineering_practice_regulation track being built in parallel and is explicitly NOT ingested here.

Prior research for this task asserted the current (1445H/2024G) edition of this regulation was 'approved at the 20th Ordinary General Assembly meeting, 2024.' This pass could NOT independently confirm that specific meeting-number attribution from a primary source: the regulation's own cover page states only 'اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الهيئة السعودية للمهندسين -- 1445هـ / 2024م' (no meeting number or exact approval date appears anywhere in the 16-page PDF), and Article 32 itself states only that the regulation takes effect 'من تاريخ إقرارها من الجمعية العمومية' (from the date of its approval by the General Assembly) without naming that date or meeting number inline. A WebSearch this pass found saudieng.sa's own news pages referring to a '21st Ordinary General Assembly' meeting whose agenda covered approving the FY2024 annual report and final accounts (consistent with Article 2(2) of this very regulation, which places the ordinary General Assembly within the three months following the Council's fiscal year end) and an older '14th Ordinary General Assembly' from a prior year -- both circumstantially consistent with, but not proof of, a '20th' meeting occurring around 2024 under the same annual numbering sequence. This track does NOT assert '20th Ordinary General Assembly, 2024' as an independently-confirmed fact; it is carried here only as an unverified prior-research claim, honestly flagged as unconfirmed by this pass's own primary-source reading.

This regulation is the Council's own consolidated CURRENT text (cover-dated 1445H/2024G); the base law's own known_unresolved_discrepancies (key saudi_engineers_implementing_regs_charter_not_ingested) had already flagged its existence without fetching it. A Wayback CDX query this pass for the exact URL saudieng.sa/Admin/NPSCERules/sce-executive-regulations.pdf returned exactly ONE archived capture (20250625074825, 25 Jun 2025) -- no earlier-dated snapshot of this file, and no earlier-dated alternate URL for a predecessor edition of this SAME instrument, was located. Because no prior edition's text could be independently fetched and diffed article-by-article, this track cannot respons‌ibly mark any individual article as 'معدلة' (amended) relative to an unverified earlier edition -- doing so would require guessing at what the prior text said. All 32 articles are therefore recorded as 'اصلية', meaning: verified as the CURRENT, single, in-force consolidated text as hosted by the regulator, NOT a claim that this text is identical, word-for-word, to whatever internal edition(s) preceded the 1445H/2024G reissuance referenced in this document's own cover date. This differs from the base law's own BOE-changelog-driven per-article amendment tracking (Articles 1 and 6 there), which was possible only because BOE's own page separately exposed a 'تعديلات المادة' popup quoting prior/superseding text -- no equivalent mechanism exists for this Council-internal, non-BOE-catalogued regulation.

Per the task brief's suggested fallback chain (direct fetch, then Wayback Machine, then a Scribd mirror, then r.jina.ai as a reader-proxy fallback), this pass attempted: (1) a direct curl fetch of https://www.saudieng.sa/Admin/NPSCERules/sce-executive-regulations.pdf, which failed with a TLS connection reset (consistent with this corpus's established pattern of saudieng.sa blocking direct scraping); (2) the Wayback Machine, which succeeded on the FIRST and ONLY archived snapshot (20250625074825, confirmed via the CDX metadata API before fetching the content-serving path, per this environment's documented CDX-works/content-path-sometimes-blocked asymmetry -- in this instance the content-serving path DID succeed via direct curl over the pre-configured proxy); (3) a WebSearch for a Scribd mirror of this specific regulation, which surfaced only Scribd/qanoonsa/lexis mirrors of the DISTINCT engineering_practice_regulation instrument (see sce_reg_disambiguation_from_engineering_practice_regulation above), not of this track's own instrument -- no Scribd mirror of THIS regulation was located; (4) r.jina.ai, which returned HTTP 401 ('blocked from performing anonymous queries due to bad IP reputation') for this URL. Because the Wayback fetch (step 2) succeeded and was independently cross-extracted by two separate PDF-parsing pipelines (poppler's pdftotext and pdfminer-based pdfplumber, the latter requiring a from-scratch bidi/glyph-order reconstruction documented in this track's generator script) that agreed on the full 32-article text byte-for-byte after normalization, this track treats the text as adequately verified despite the Scribd/r.jina.ai fallbacks being unavailable this pass, consistent with the corpus's 1-2-verification-attempts-per-fact policy.

This PDF consistently uses an informal hamza-under-alef orthographic style for a class of common words that formal MSA legal drafting would normally spell with a plain alef or alef-wasl (e.g. 'إجتماع/الإجتماعات' for 'اجتماع', 'إنتخابات/الإنتخابية' for 'انتخابات/الانتخابية', 'إعتراض' for 'اعتراض', 'إستثنائية' for 'استثنائية', 'إستيفاء' for 'استيفاء', 'إفتتاح' for 'افتتاح') -- but does so INCONSISTENTLY even within the same document (e.g. Article 9's 'مبني' clause and the Chapter-3 sub-heading 'ج. أسلوب الانتخاب' both use the plain, hamza-free spelling 'الانتخاب/الانتخابية' in the same breath as hamza-bearing 'الإنتخابات' elsewhere). This track preserves EVERY instance exactly as it appears in the two independently cross-checked extractions, article by article, rather than silently normalizing spelling to a single consistent house style -- per this corpus's no-silent-correction policy. Separately, THREE genuine, narrower one-off spelling artifacts were confirmed identically by both independent extraction pipelines and are preserved verbatim rather than corrected: (a) Article 2, item 5: 'الأعضاء الأساسين' (missing an internal 'ي'; standard spelling would be 'الأساسيين'); (b) Article 6, item 3: 'رئيس مجلس الادارة' (missing the hamza used everywhere else in this document for 'الإدارة'); (c) Article 22: 'يتم إجراء القرعه بينهم' ('القرعه' spelled with a plain 'ه' rather than tied 'ة', standard spelling 'القرعة').

Article 29, within item 2's sentence, both independently-run extraction pipelines (pdftotext -layout via poppler, and a from-scratch bidi-corrected pdfplumber/pdfminer word-level reconstruction, verified down to individual PDF glyph tokens and their x/y coordinates) agree EXACTLY on an anomalous embedded token reading '-3٣' (an ASCII '3' immediately followed by an Arabic-Indic '٣', both attached to a dash) sitting in the middle of item 2's own sentence, between '...والخطابات.' and 'تقديم المشورة الفنية في المجالات الهندسية.' -- i.e. what should read as one sentence for item 2 ('الاعتماد والتصديق للوثائق والمستندات والتوقيعات والخطابات، وتقديم المشورة الفنية في المجالات الهندسية.') instead carries a stray, duplicated numeral marker mid-sentence, while the NEXT item is separately (and normally) labeled '3- تدريب وتأهيل المهندسين والفنيين.' -- meaning the numeral '3' effectively appears twice in immediate succession for two different pieces of text. Because this artifact is confirmed identically by two structurally-independent parsing pipelines operating on the same archived primary PDF (ruling out a tool-specific OCR/extraction error), it is treated as a genuine typesetting anomaly in the Council's own source document and is preserved VERBATIM in this track's ingested text for Article 29 (rather than silently deleted, renumbered, or 'corrected' into a clean item 3), per this corpus's binding no-fabrication/no-silent-correction rule. It cannot be determined from this pass whether the Council's own drafters intended the 'تقديم المشورة الفنية...' clause to be a separate item (in which case every subsequent item from 3 onward would arguably be off-by-one relative to the Council's own original numbering intent) or whether it is simply a leftover, meaningless duplicate-digit typesetting artifact; this track does not guess and instead preserves the anomaly with this explicit flag.

Two further Council-issued instruments were identified this pass via the same Wayback CDX directory listing (saudieng.sa/Admin/NPSCERules/) but are NOT ingested in this track, consistent with this corpus's one-instrument-per-pass precedent: (1) sce-board-of-directors-work-rules.pdf ('قواعد عمل مجلس الإدارة' -- Board of Directors' own internal work rules/procedures, a Board-level instrument distinct from this General-Assembly-approved executive regulation, archived 15 Jun 2025); (2) SCESystem.pdf, which appears to be the Council's own PDF hosting of the BASE LAW text itself (already tracked separately in this corpus at sources/saudi_engineers/) rather than a distinct instrument. An English-language translation of this exact regulation (sce-executive-regulations-en.pdf, archived 13 Feb 2026) was also located but not used for anything beyond confirming the Arabic file's own English-language sibling exists; per this corpus's binding rule that Arabic is the sole governing source, the English PDF was not fetched, read, or used to inform or correct any Arabic wording in this track.
